The service is very friendly

text.text:
One star because the parking system is extremely chaotic. Visitors are forced to pay twice: at the entrance and to the illegal parking attendants who direct their vehicles.

Despite the "no tipping" sign, there are still additional fees. When questioned, the illegal parking attendants simply reply, "If you don't want to pay, just park inside the building."

The parking attendants also don't wear official uniforms, further increasing the uncertainty of the legality and regulations.

If there really is a "no tipping" sign, it should be consistently enforced, not just written down.

What is the purpose of paying for parking at the entrance if there are still other fees?

This situation is very uncomfortable and detrimental to visitors.

It's unfortunate that, at a time when businesses are trying to expand in this area, something as basic as the parking system is being poorly managed.

The parking system needs to be improved and regulated.

originalText.text:
Bintang 1 karena sistem parkir sangat kacau. Pengunjung dipaksa membayar dua kali: di gerbang masuk dan kepada tukang parkir liar yang mengatur kendaraan.

Padahal terdapat spanduk bertuliskan “no tipping”, namun kenyataannya tetap ada pungutan tambahan. Saat ditanyakan, tukang parkir liar justru menjawab, “kalau tidak mau bayar, parkir saja di dalam gedung.”

Tukang parkir juga tidak menggunakan seragam resmi, sehingga semakin tidak jelas legalitas dan aturan yang berlaku.

Jika memang “no tipping”, seharusnya ditegakkan dengan konsisten, bukan hanya sekadar tulisan.

Apa fungsi pembayaran parkir di pintu masuk jika masih ada pungutan lain?

Situasi ini sangat tidak nyaman dan merugikan pengunjung.

Sangat disayangkan, di saat ingin mengembangkan usaha di area ini, hal mendasar seperti sistem parkir justru dikelola dengan buruk.

Sistem parkir nya harus diperbaiki dan ditertibkan.

My weekend night adventure led me to Gulai Tikungan, a bustling eatery located in a densely populated area. The journey here was an adventure in itself; due to the campaign happening at the moment, it involved some walking. When I finally reached the restaurant, the atmosphere was electric, mirroring the surrounding neighborhood.

As a testament to its popularity, the place was brimming with customers. I ordered their signature dish, the “gultik,” and was pleasantly surprised by the speedy service, considering the crowds. However, my enthusiasm was met with a bit of a letdown when the portion size was revealed. In my case, as I’m not accustomed to consuming large meals at night, it sufficed. But for those with heartier appetites, you might need to order multiple servings to fill your belly.

Gulai Tikungan is known for its affordability, which is quite a bonus considering its reputation. While the taste, in my opinion, didn’t venture into the realm of extraordinary, it was undeniably good, boasting those familiar, comforting flavors.

In conclusion, Gulai Tikungan thrives in its popularity and reasonable prices, though you might have to adjust your expectations regarding portion sizes. It’s a gem for a quick, basic, and satisfying meal amidst the bustling energy of the area.

Strategically located near the Blok M transport hub, within reasonable walking distances from the Blok M MRT station and the TransJakarta bus terminal. Luckily, the servers did a great job on placing and preparing the orders, as well as processing the many payments. They accept cash, cards, and online payment methods.

text.text:
Blok M can get really crowded even on weekdays, so plan your visit accordingly. I arrived at 11:45 AM and the place was already packed, waiting about 15 minutes to be seated. The restaurant itself is tiny and tucked away in a hidden spot just beneath the entrance staircase, but trust me, it’s absolutely worth the search.

I ordered the Ayam Lada Hitam, Ayam Teriyaki, Bayam Crispy, and Udang Mentega. The seasoning across the board was spot on. The Ayam Lada Hitam is a definite must-order, bold, punchy, and perfectly seasoned with chicken that was tender all the way through. The Udang Mentega was okay. The Ayam Teriyaki had a really tasty sauce, but the chicken meat itself was too thin. With a bit of adjustment it could be a great dish. The one other letdown was the Bayam Crispy, which came out a little too salty for my taste.

Despite the crowd, the service was impressively quick and efficient. If you’re in the Blok M area and don’t mind a little hustle to get a seat, Kedai Penuh Nikmat is well worth it. Just come early! 🙌

For me its worth the wait when i can go buy and other things at Blok M while waiting.

Finally tried Zibaa Kafe and I absolutely loved it. The vibrant energy of this Middle Eastern spot really stands out—bold colors, eclectic details, and warm lighting create a lively, bazaar-like atmosphere that feels both playful and well-curated.

Cheesy, generously filled, and simply comforting.

Juicy and tender with a crunchy coating, well-seasoned in a Middle Eastern style, paired with their aioli-like sauce—really good.
- Muhalabia
Almost like a panna cotta, Middle Eastern style—slightly citrusy with a fragrant rosewater aroma that’s not overly perfumey. Rich, silky, and creamy.

Overall, a very satisfying experience—great flavors, warm ambiance, and definitely worth coming back for.

Stopping by Ayam Bolo Bebek (Chicken Bolo Duck) is on our to-do list. When we arrived, there were no other customers. After we sat down to order, another customer did too.
We ordered the Special Package (Gendaan). This package is for two: 1 fried chicken
1 fried baby
2 rice dishes
tofu with milk
Stir-fried water spinach
Iced lemon tea/lychee tea

Bebek Ganas and white rice: This duck is like smashed duck, then coated with chili sauce. For me, the duck is very tender, and the chili sauce is very spicy, unfortunately, the chili sauce is salty and tends to be bitter. I couldn't taste anything else, whether it was salty or sweet, but it was just salty and bitter, and the spiciness was quite strong.

To serve two, the chicken and duck are fried dry and taste delicious. For the rice order, there's serundeng (fried coconut), sliced ​​cucumber, red and green chili sauce, and green spices (like Madura spices), and there's crispy fried eggplant.

The tofu with milk is soft and has a salty flavor. The fresh kale was still crunchy when cooked, and it tasted delicious, savory, salty, and a little sweet. There were also sliced ​​onions.

Overall, I'd come back here to try other dishes. In my opinion, there should be a choice of domestic chicken, male chicken, or kampung chicken, with a reasonable price. The chicken was very small when it came out. The lady told me it was a small kampung chicken, so for a single chicken of that size, priced at 26,000 Rupiah, it's definitely overpriced.

The place is cool, clean, and air-conditioned. The service is fast and friendly.

text.text:
Soto Betawi Bang Ebet hidden gem that’s absolutely worth the queue! Not located on the main road, but don’t let that fool you… this place is packed. Long waiting list, people sitting outside, and honestly at first I was thinking, “Is it really worth the hype?” Then the food came… and now I totally get it. 😆

For me, the star here is definitely their Soto Betawi + Oseng Daging Santan at around 43k. The broth is rich, comforting, and flavorful without being too heavy. Pair it with rice (8k) and it becomes the perfect comfort meal. This is personally my favorite combo. also i order soicy level 3 (they’ll ask you what do you want for the spicy level i think from 0 to 5/6)

If you enjoy jeroan/intestines, then don’t miss the Oseng Campur version many people around us were ordering it too.

For add-ons, we tried:
✨ Sate Paru Goreng (3 tusuk) 30k, really good texture and flavorful
✨ Sate Kikil (3 tusuk) 27k, chewy in a good way and surprisingly addictive
✨ Kerupuk Kaleng Coklat 4.5k each, simple but somehow makes the whole meal even better 😄

And trust me, es teh tawar refill (8k) is the best combo here. Something about that cold unsweetened tea just balances the richness of the soto perfectly.

Pro tips:
If the queue is long (which most likely it will be 😆), don’t panic. You can actually sit next door at Nasi Uduk Kribo, just order a drink from them while waiting. Makes the waiting experience much more comfortable.

Also, if you choose the outdoor seating area, they may ask for payment in advance just a heads up so you’re not surprised.

Definitely recommended and yes… this is one of those places that once you try it, you’ll understand why people are willing to queue. Will be back for sure. AMAZING!!!

text.text:
Pasar Modern BSD is a vibrant culinary destination that offers a delightful mix of traditional flavors and modern food stalls. My recent visit led me to two standout spots — Bakmi Prima and Early Kopitiam — both of which delivered memorable, satisfying meals. The market’s casual, open-air atmosphere makes it an enjoyable place to stroll, snack, and soak in the local vibe.

Bakmi Prima served one of the best bakso goreng I’ve ever had, crispy and full of flavor, while Early Kopitiam brought comforting breakfast classics like kaya toast and strong local coffee in a warm, nostalgic setting. Both places had their own charm, and the quality of the food exceeded expectations for such a humble setting. It’s the kind of spot where good food doesn’t have to shout — it speaks through taste.

What’s exciting is that I’ve only scratched the surface. Pasar Modern BSD seems full of hidden gems just waiting to be discovered — from noodle stalls and coffee shops to local desserts and street-style snacks. I’ll definitely be back to explore more. If you enjoy authentic, affordable food with heart, this place is well worth a visit.

text.text:
Bumbu Pekalongan is a cozy spot in Gading Serpong that serves delicious Javanese dishes, especially specialties from Pekalongan. Their signature menu includes Nasi Megono (young jackfruit with rice) and Tauto (a unique take on soto using tauco or fermented soy sauce) — both flavorful and something different from your usual Indonesian food!

I tried the Tauto and fried chicken, and it really hit the spot. The taste is bold, comforting, and has that homey vibe. The place is usually pretty packed, which says a lot about the food quality.

Price-wise, it’s a bit on the pricier side, but still reasonable considering the taste and portion. Worth trying if you’re curious about authentic Central Javanese flavors!
